guidance: Planning arithmetic for a linear commit range. The step count assumes exactly one first-bad commit, no skipped commits and no merges in the range; reproduce the failure before marking a commit, and close the session with git bisect reset.
method: git bisect is a binary search. The candidates are the commits reachable from the bad revision and not from the good one, counted by git rev-list --count good..bad; exactly one of them is the first bad commit and every older candidate is good. Any binary search over N ordered items needs at most ceil(log2 N) probes, the smallest k with 2^k >= N, because each probe discards at least half of the remaining candidates: 0 tests for 1 commit, 1 for 2, 2 for 3 or 4, 3 for 5 to 8, 7 for 100, 10 for 1,000 and 20 for 1,000,000, against up to N - 1 tests when the commits are walked one by one from the good end. Each row tests the candidate at index floor((n - 1) / 2) of the current n-commit range, counting from the oldest, which cuts the range into a lower block of floor((n - 1) / 2) + 1 commits, the tested commit and everything older, and an upper block of n - 1 - floor((n - 1) / 2) commits. A bad answer keeps the lower block because the tested commit may itself be the culprit, and a good answer keeps the upper block, so the larger block holds ceil(n / 2) commits and the depth is exactly ceil(log2 n). The table follows that larger, older block after every bad answer, the branch that spends the full number of tests, and its Left if good and Left if bad columns are the candidates left in each case. An even candidate count leaves two equally balanced middle commits and git may test either, which does not change the depth. A commit skipped with git bisect skip costs one extra test, because git must find another probe, and a merged history is bisected correctly but the count covers every commit in the range rather than a straight line. The page accepts a count from 1 to 1,000,000 or a list of up to 5,000 pasted git log --reverse --oneline lines, which replaces the count and lets every row name a real commit; a line may carry a 4 to 40 digit hex abbreviation and a subject, and leading graph bullets and blank lines are dropped. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
